text: Given a site with one ONLINE, one OFFLINE, and one UPDATING device, when unifi_list_device_issues is called, then issues contains exactly the OFFLINE device (tagged offline) and the UPDATING device (tagged transitioning), and excludes the ONLINE device
Given a device that is both OFFLINE and has firmwareUpdatable: true, when the tool is called, then that device's issue_types contains both offline and firmware_update_available
Given a site where every device is ONLINE with firmwareUpdatable: false, when the tool is called, then it returns issues: [] with a normal success response, not an error

Given a site_id the upstream API does not recognize, when the tool is called, then it returns the same structured error envelope (not_found or invalid_argument) unifi_list_devices would return for the same bad site_id, not an unhandled exception

Given a request to unifi_list_device_issues with the X-Unifi-Api-Key / X-Unifi-Console-Id headers missing, when the tool is called, then it returns the exact NO_TOKEN error envelope every other tool returns in the same situation

Given a site with 260 devices (upstream page size 200), when the tool is called with the default max_devices, then issues reflects devices from both upstream pages, scanned equals 260, and truncated is false
Given a site with 900 devices and max_devices=500 (default), when the tool is called, then scanned equals 500, truncated is true, and the tool does not error or hang

Given two concurrent calls to unifi_list_device_issues using two different X-Unifi-Api-Key/X-Unifi-Console-Id header pairs pointing at two different consoles, when both run concurrently, then each caller's issues only contains devices from its own console, verified at the header/credential level
